positions.name: Keysight Technologies, Inc.
positions.catalyst: Q3 FY26 reported after the close YESTERDAY (Aug 18) and it was a blowout on every line. Revenue $1.846B, +36% y/y. Orders a record $2.091B, +56% y/y — the first $2B order quarter in company history. Non-GAAP EPS $3.07, +79% y/y and roughly a 24% beat vs consensus. Commercial communications crossed $1B of revenue for the first time ever and wireline revenue exceeded wireless for the first time in company history, with wireline orders more than doubling y/y on AI data-center buildout. Guidance was raised, not just met: Q4 revenue $1.930-1.950B (+37% y/y at the midpoint) and Q4 EPS $3.34-3.40 (+76% y/y at the midpoint); full-year FY26 lifted to ~$7.103B revenue (+32%) and ~$11.48 non-GAAP EPS (+60%).
positions.driver: This is the cleanest under-reaction on the tape. KEYS was dumped into the print — it opened Aug 18 at $349.96, traded down to $332.64 intraday in the semiconductor/AI unwind, and closed $341.00 — and is only bid ~$350.7 pre-market, +2.9%. So a 24% EPS beat, record orders and a full-year raise have bought the stock roughly nothing beyond recovering one bad session; it still sits ~6% below its $374.96 June 52-week high. Gap risk is already spent, so there is nothing to chase, and the invalidation is unambiguous: a $329.68 stop (6%) sits below yesterday's $332.64 low, i.e. below the entire capitulation range. Against that, yesterday's $350.90 high is the only overhead level before open air toward $365-375. Compared with today's other catalysts this is the best skew — Estée Lauder is a genuine beat-and-raise but is already +7% pre-market (buying the top of the gap, where a gap-fill is a stop-out), Target is -3.6% and Lowe's -1.9% on their prints, TJX had not released as of the run, and ADI reports after the close.
positions.risks: KEYS is levered to AI and semiconductor capex, which is exactly what is being unwound — a second down day in SMH/AI infrastructure can drag KEYS lower regardless of its own numbers, and that is the single biggest threat to this trade. Management flagged supply-chain constraints limiting the ability to convert record orders into revenue, which is the bear hook analysts will press on and which caps how much of that $2.09B backlog is real near-term revenue. The stock already carries a ~59x trailing P/E and has run from $152.85 (Aug 2025 low) to $375, so a lot of the AI test-demand story is priced; a 'good but priced in' verdict would leave it flat-to-down. Broader tape is unhelpful — yields and oil climbing, the ceasefire lapsed, and FOMC minutes land this afternoon, any of which can produce a risk-off session that overwhelms a single company's print. Finally, an under-reaction can simply mean the market disagrees.
